title: Fast Times, Slow Times: Timescale Separation in Financial Timeseries Data
hypothesis: Financial timeseries contain slow and fast components separable by variance and tail stationarity (generalized eigenvalue/tICA problems); in-sample slow-component timescales persist out-of-sample.
data_sources: G10 currencies - instrument list, source, frequency, price vs return definition not stated
Five multifactor equity ETFs: IFSU, IUSZ, IUVL, IUMO, IUQA
US Treasuries - maturities/instruments, source, frequency not stated
sample: Three separate baskets analyzed independently. No explicit N observations, N periods count, or data source printed. Filters not stated. Only basket composition and time windows are printed.
period_start: not stated as single calendar date - multiple fit/OOS windows: G10 2006-2010 fit, 2010-2025 OOS; ETFs 2021-2022 fit, 2022-2025 OOS; Treasuries 1994-1998 fit, 1998-2025 OOS
period_end: not stated as single calendar date - see windows above
method: 1. Define X_t = n-dim column vector process (paper: e.g. prices or returns - which used for which basket not stated; demeaning, frequency, handling of missing/holidays not stated).

2. Linear tICA (k=1, sec 2.1): minimize d/dt Var(X_t w_i^T) s.t. Var(W X_t^T)=1. Leads to generalized eigenvalue problem C(t,T) w = lambda C(t,0) w where C(t,T)=1/2 E[X_{t+T}^T X_t + X_t^T X_{t+T}] is lag-T autocovariance, C(t,0)=E[X_t^T X_t] covariance, lambda=(1+beta)/2T. C(t,0) real symmetric positive definite. Solve with LAPACK gvd or scipy.linalg.eigh. Eigenvalues lambda_i in [-1,1] are autocorrelations. Timescales t_i = -2T / (lambda_i -1). Lag T value, discretization of dX_t, expectation estimator not stated.

3. Tail tICA (k=4, sec 2.2): minimize drift of 2k-th moment (1/2k)E(X_t w^T)^{2k} s.t. E[w_i X_t^T X_t w_j^T]=delta_ij. Solution satisfies (2k-1)E[(X_t w^T)^{2k-2}(dX_t w^T)X_t]+E[(X_t w^T)^{2k-1}dX_t]=beta w, w^T w=1, beta=2kE[(X_t w^T)^{2k-1}(dX_t w^T)]=2k d/dt M_{2k}, lambda=E[(X_t w^T)^{2k-1}(X_{t+T} w^T)] tail autocorrelation order k.

4. Numerics for k=4: Fixed Point Iteration (FastICA). Single: w <- E[X_t d(w^T X_t)^{2k-1})] - (2k-1)E[(w^T X_t)^{2k-2}] w ; w <- w/|w|. Parallel: W <- E[X_t d(W^T X_t)^{2k-1})] - (2k-1)E[(W^T X_t)^{2k-2}] W ; W <- (W X_t^T X_t W^T)^(-1/2) W. Initialization, convergence tolerance, restarts not stated.

5. Empirical windows - parameters (not results): G10: fit 2006-2010 extract slowest components, project 2010-2025 OOS. ETFs: fit 2021-2022 extract slowest components, project 2022-2025 OOS. Treasuries: fit 1994-1998, continuation 1998-2025. k=1 linear and k=4 nonlinear fitted per basket. Increasing k beyond 4 did not produce further meaningful changes - no threshold printed.

6. Extraction: 5 slowest components extracted for G10 and ETF baskets (explicit). Number for Treasuries not stated - figures show 5 but text does not state. Eigenvectors = directions of fastest/slowest decay. Weights rescaled to unit gross exposure (sum |w|=1).

7. OOS projection: apply in-sample weights w to OOS X_t to obtain Y_t = X_t w^T; plot in-sample green background vs OOS white background as Figures 1-3. Assessment is visual: no visible deterioration at in-sample to OOS transition; where higher frequencies enter due to 2008-2010 GFC or 2023 geopolitical events components revert to original slow timescale; orthogonality decays as expected out-of-sample. No numeric table, test statistic, p-value or standard error printed.

8. Theoretical benchmarks: eigenvalues in [-1,1]; unit gross exposure =1. Flash Crash 2010 S&P 500 -9% cited as background example, not estimate from this analysis. Data frequency, return definition, T, covariance estimation window, significance test not stated.
